proposals.evidence: DEDR 3655 lists Tamil nāl/nālu/nāṉku, Malayalam nālu, Kannada nāku/nālku, Telugu nālugu, Gondi nāluŋ and Kurukh nāx ‘four’. These exact numeral responses are not confused with the day-word nāḷ. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 3263(a) lists Tamil tiṉ, Kannada tin/tinu/tinnu and the widespread cognate eating verb; Kannada past stem tind- and related inflection belong here. Causatives, food derivatives and subsection (b) right-hand expressions are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 2426 explicitly compares Tamil cā, Kannada sāy (past sattu), Gondi hā-/sāy-, Kurux khē’enā (keccas), Malto keye and Brahui kahing die. Only the intransitive verb is proposed here; derived causative kill responses require a distinct relation analysis. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
